title: U.S. House · Nevada's 2nd District
area: Northern Nevada, including Reno, Sparks, Carson City, and most of the state's rural counties.

context.text: This is the only open U.S. House seat in Nevada in 2026: incumbent Mark Amodei (R) retired from public office rather than seek re-election. Twenty-four candidates (11 Democrats, 13 Republicans) filed for the seat, the most of any Nevada district. Teresa Benitez-Thompson, a former Nevada Assembly majority leader, won the Democratic primary; David Flippo, a retired U.S. Air Force officer, won the Republican primary.

candidates.name: Teresa Benitez-Thompson

summary.text: Teresa Benitez-Thompson is the Democratic nominee for the open U.S. House Nevada District 2 seat. A licensed clinical social worker who worked in adoption and hospice care, she served in the Nevada Assembly for more than a decade, including as majority floor leader, and later became chief of staff to Attorney General Aaron Ford. She has said her priorities include funding for SNAP, Medicaid, tribal communities and veterans.

background.text: Born in Ventura, California, and moved with her family to Nevada at age 4, according to the Nevada Independent; she grew up in Reno and is of Mexican descent.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from the University of Nevada, Reno, and a master's degree in social work from the University of Michigan.
Was crowned Miss Nevada in 2002 and competed in the Miss America pageant, according to the Nevada Independent, which reports she funded her undergraduate education in part with pageant scholarships.

Worked as a social worker for five years helping with adoptions of children with special needs, then for about a decade with terminally ill patients as a hospice social worker, per the Nevada Independent.

Won election to the Nevada Assembly, District 27 (Washoe County), in November 2010 and represented it until leaving office in 2022; the Nevada Independent describes her as the Assembly's first Latina majority leader.

Served as Assembly Majority Floor Leader from 2017 to 2019 according to the Nevada Legislature, with committee service that included Health and Human Services, Taxation, Revenue (vice chair in 2021) and Ways and Means (vice chair in 2019); she chaired the Government Affairs Committee in 2013.

Legislative work highlighted by the Nevada Independent includes advocacy for WC-1, the 2016 Washoe County ballot measure that raised the sales tax for school construction, and a 2017 law requiring insurers to cover 12 months of contraception without a copay.

Did not seek re-election in 2022 because of term limits; later served as chief of staff to Attorney General Aaron Ford, and announced her congressional run in 2026 after Rep. Mark Amodei announced his retirement. She won the Democratic primary on June 9, 2026.
Is married to Jeff Thompson; Ballotpedia lists three children, while the Nevada Independent quotes her as a mother of four.

positions.summary: Voted yes on AB 456, which raised Nevada's minimum wage in steps to $12 an hour by 2024.
Voted yes on SB 143, which required background checks on private firearm sales and transfers.
In a Nevada Independent questionnaire she said Congress should not pass the SAVE America Act, citing states' authority to hold elections.
positions.quote: Every eligible American has the right to vote and nothing should come between that right and the opportunity to exercise that right,

positions.summary: In a Nevada Independent questionnaire she answered "mostly no" on deporting all undocumented immigrants and criticized the administration's mass deportation policy, calling for reform with humane enforcement.
positions.quote: We've seen needless deaths and chaos resulting from this administration's hardline mass deportation policy

positions.summary: In a Nevada Independent questionnaire she agreed that President Trump's tariffs have harmed Nevada.
positions.quote: The courts have struck down multiple illegal applications of tariffs, yet the tariffs keep coming,

positions.summary: In a Nevada Independent questionnaire she answered yes to reinstating Affordable Care Act premium subsidies and no to the Medicaid work requirements.
positions.quote: When people can't afford insurance, it means the only form of medical care they can access are the emergency rooms.

record.text: Served on the Nevada Assembly Health and Human Services, Revenue (vice chair), and Ways and Means committees during the 2021-2022 session.
Voted yes on AB 456 (raising Nevada's minimum wage in steps to $12 an hour, or $11 for employers offering health insurance, by 2024), which passed the Assembly 28-12 on May 28, 2019.
Voted yes on SB 143 (requiring background checks on private firearm sales and transfers), which passed the Assembly 28-13 on February 15, 2019.

Voted yes on SB 551 (eliminating a scheduled reduction in the Modified Business Tax on employers to fund an additional $98 million for K-12 education), which passed the Assembly 28-13 on June 3, 2019.

candidates.researchNotes: SB 551's Modified Business Tax increase applies broadly to Nevada employers of varying size (the floor debate cited impacts on thousands of small businesses), not specifically high earners or corporations, so it was not used as a tax_wealthy position despite the vote itself being verified accurate.

summary.text: David Flippo is the Republican nominee for the open U.S. House Nevada District 2 seat. A retired U.S. Air Force lieutenant colonel, he later worked for BP in Alaska, became a financial advisor and owns a HobbyTown store. He moved to District 2 this election cycle and won the Republican primary with an endorsement from President Donald Trump.

background.text: Born in Maryland and graduated from Christiansburg High School, according to Ballotpedia.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Montana State University (1991) and a graduate degree from Valdosta State University (1995).

Served in the U.S. Air Force from 1985 to 2009 and retired as a lieutenant colonel. According to his campaign, he commanded more than 1,000 personnel, stood up three combat bases in Iraq, and led maintenance operations at Eielson Air Force Base, Alaska; his Ballotpedia survey says he commanded two squadrons there overseeing 800 Airmen.
After retiring from the Air Force, worked for BP in Alaska for 10 years on a preventive-maintenance program for the North Slope oilfield and the Alaska Pipeline.
Later became a licensed financial advisor in Las Vegas and owns a HobbyTown retail store, per his survey and the Nevada Independent.

Ballotpedia lists him as a 2026 candidate for Nevada's 4th District who did not appear on that district's June 9 primary ballot; the Associated Press reports he moved to the 2nd District this election cycle after losing a race in southern Nevada in 2024.

Won the June 9, 2026 Republican primary in District 2 after President Donald Trump endorsed him in the closing weeks, over former state Sen. James Settelmeyer, who was backed by Gov. Joe Lombardo and retiring Rep. Mark Amodei.
Says on his campaign website that he is a Christian, husband of 42 years, father and grandfather; his Ballotpedia survey says he and his wife, Dawn, live in Nevada.

priorities.text: Border security: strengthen border enforcement, increase resources for Border Patrol, and deploy technology and infrastructure including finishing the border wall.
Economic growth: oppose tax increases, cut wasteful government spending, reduce regulations on small business, and strengthen supply chains.
Military and veterans: ensure defense funding keeps forces ready, and expand healthcare, mental health support, and job opportunities for veterans.

positions.summary: In a Nevada Independent questionnaire he answered "mostly yes" to deporting all undocumented immigrants, saying deportations are necessary and should put the needs of American citizens first.
positions.quote: Deportations are necessary to ease the housing demand and make job salaries more competitive for American workers, especially in the construction trades.

positions.summary: Says he will oppose any attempt to restrict the Second Amendment and defend the rights of law-abiding Americans to keep and bear arms.
positions.quote: I will oppose any attempt to restrict the Second Amendment and always defend the rights of law-abiding Americans to protect themselves, their families, and their communities.

positions.summary: Says he will oppose any and all tax increases and lower taxes whenever possible.
positions.quote: Oppose any and all tax increases and lower taxes whenever possible

positions.summary: In a Nevada Independent questionnaire, his campaign said Congress should pass the SAVE America Act.
positions.quote: Congress should absolutely pass the SAVE America Act.

positions.summary: In a Nevada Independent questionnaire he answered no to reinstating Affordable Care Act premium subsidies and yes to Medicaid work requirements.
positions.quote: Obamacare was a disaster for the American people, specifically Nevadans

candidates.name: Lynn Chapman

summary.text: Lynn Chapman is the Independent American Party candidate for U.S. House Nevada District 2 and the party's treasurer in Nevada. Chapman also ran for the seat in 2024, finishing third with about 5 percent of the vote. Little other biographical information is publicly available.

background.text: The Nevada Independent's 2026 voter guide lists Chapman as treasurer of the Nevada Independent American Party.
Ran for U.S. House Nevada District 2 in 2024 as an Independent American Party candidate, receiving 19,784 votes (5.0 percent) in the general election won by incumbent Mark Amodei.

candidates.researchNotes: Searched campaign, Ballotpedia (no Candidate Connection survey), news and voter-guide sources in October 2026; found no campaign website, platform or public statements by Lynn Chapman.
